candidate.review: Use the reviewed source and any pinned runtime evidence to trace ordinary success and failure, repetition, cancellation, abandonment, deferred work, and reuse. State the initial conditions and order the steps that determine the outcome. Compare both event orders and test intervening operations before treating an earlier event as decisive. Follow each completion from admission through reporting, state refresh, and effect. Check whether an obsolete report can be discarded even when cleanup or error propagation continues. Distinguish rebinding a caller's reference from replacing the value through the captured reference, and use an unchanged reference as a control. Check whether registration actually succeeds after a state observation, and keep notification, suspension, lock reacquisition, and return distinct. Compare notifications before and after registration, and distinguish when a lock is required to change the condition or begin waiting from when it is optional for notification. Preserve controls for copying before and after first use, cleanup after normal and abrupt exit, and valid reuse after earlier waiters return. Qualify exceptional behavior by the documented exclusions, compatibility mode, and whether a prior association is still present. Separate deadline calculation from dispatch and delivery. Compare repeated cancellation, expiry, and reactivation in order, checking the current state and whether earlier work has started, finished, or can overlap later work. For queued work, trace availability checks, enqueue, handoff, and shutdown through later callers and subsequent returns. Check who receives an available resource, what eventually releases the older waiter, and which validation runs on each path. Distinguish invoking cleanup from establishing its effect, and preserving error text from preserving error identity. Cite the branches, tests, and contract language that support each claim, and qualify conclusions by source coverage, version, configuration, and supported input range. Leave intent OPEN where the evidence does not settle transition timing, duplicate or abandoned completion, counter refresh and numeric limits, ownership or copying, exceptional exits, notification analogies, delivery guarantees, queue ordering, validation, or shutdown obligations. Where contract statements appear inconsistent, identify the event order and scope that expose the conflict and leave the intended wording OPEN.

findings.text: Start with a false condition, a caller holding c.L, and no registered waiters. A notifier may call Signal or Broadcast without c.L. If it does so before Wait registers, even after the caller observed the false condition, that notification wakes nobody and the caller needs a later notification. If Wait registers first and notification arrives before the call to runtime_notifyListWait, the documented atomic wait requires that notification to count for the registered waiter. Ticket handling is delegated to the runtime. Observing or changing the condition and entering Wait require c.L.
findings.question: OPEN: Should the channel analogy explicitly say that each Cond notification applies to the waiters registered at that point, including for Broadcast?

findings.text: With multiple waiters on the same Cond, a notifier can acquire c.L, change the condition, call Signal, and release c.L. Signal unblocks one waiter and synchronizes before the Wait it unblocks. The waiter must then acquire c.L before returning. Another contender can acquire c.L first and change the condition again, so the returning caller checks the condition under c.L and waits again if it is false.

citation.fragment: they may be awoken before a "waiting" goroutine.

findings.text: With multiple waiters already registered, a caller holding c.L can change the condition and call Broadcast. Broadcast unblocks all current waiters. Each Wait returns after its caller reacquires c.L. Once those callers have returned and released c.L, another caller can acquire it and use the same Cond to wait on a false condition. Its Wait needs a new Signal or Broadcast.

citation.fragment: Broadcast wakes all goroutines waiting on c.

findings.text: Start with a fresh Cond from NewCond and a pointer-valued Locker. A value copy made before either Cond is used has a zero checker and can initialize its checker at its own address on first use. Both Cond values still refer to the same Locker. If the original first calls Signal with no waiters and is then copied by value, the copied checker contains the original checker's address. Wait, Signal, or Broadcast on that copy panics at the check before touching its notification list. A second pointer to the original Cond still uses the original checker address.

Construct a Cond with Locker A and enter Wait holding A. Wait registers and calls Unlock on A. If c.L still contains A when the waiter resumes, Wait locks A before returning. Reassigning the caller's local Locker variable after NewCond also leaves c.L containing A. If another goroutine assigns Locker B directly to c.L after Wait unlocks A and orders the write before the notification that wakes Wait, the resumed Wait reads c.L again and calls Lock on B. If that call succeeds, Wait returns holding B.
findings.question: OPEN: Is replacing c.L during an outstanding Wait supported even with synchronization, or must the associated Locker stay fixed throughout the call?

findings.text: Start with an uncopied Cond whose custom Locker panics from Unlock. Wait passes the copy check, registers a ticket, and invokes Unlock. The panic propagates before Wait calls the runtime wait function or reaches the call to Lock. This method has no deferred ticket cleanup. Whether Unlock released the underlying lock before panicking depends on the Locker implementation, and the supplied source leaves the later fate of the ticket unresolved.
findings.question: OPEN: Does the Cond contract assume that Locker methods complete normally, or is an abandoned registration after an Unlock panic expected to be recoverable?

summary.limitation: Semantic classifications are attributed reviewer judgments, not proof of entailment.
